_note: Canonical names for the theme and technique identifiers that more than one book uses. Each book still names the idea in its own words on its own page; these are the names the glossary, the quotation explorer and the cross-library filters use, so that two books' particular slants on one term do not become two separate headings. Run `node scripts/rebuild-vocabulary.js` to see which shared identifiers still need one, and `--draft` for a starting point to edit. Entries here are curated by hand and are preserved when the draft is regenerated.

catalogue.name: Catalogue
catalogue.definition: A list allowed to run on past the point of usefulness, so that the accumulation itself becomes the effect.

dialect.name: Dialect
dialect.definition: Spelling and grammar used to mark where a speaker comes from, and what being heard that way costs them.

direct-address.name: Direct address
direct-address.definition: A narrator or speaker turning outward to address the reader or the audience by name.

disguise.name: Disguise
disguise.definition: A character concealing their identity, so that the audience knows more than the people on stage do.

double-plot.name: Double plot
double-plot.definition: A second story running beside the first, repeating its problem in another key and commenting on it.

epigram.name: Epigram
epigram.definition: A short balanced sentence that sounds like settled wisdom and usually turns a received idea inside out.

frame-narrative.name: Frame narrative
frame-narrative.definition: A story told inside another story, so that every account reaches the reader through somebody with an interest in it.

gothic.name: Gothic machinery
gothic.definition: The stock furniture of Gothic writing — the ruin, the storm, the locked room, the buried secret — put to a particular use.

idiolect.name: Idiolect
idiolect.definition: A speech habit belonging to one character alone, so that they can be recognised before they are named.

landscape.name: Landscape
landscape.definition: Place and weather made to press on the people living in them, rather than serving as scenery.

prophecy.name: Prophecy
prophecy.definition: A statement about the future that shapes the action by being believed, whether or not it is true.

retrospective-narration.name: Retrospective narration
retrospective-narration.definition: A narrator telling their own earlier life, with the distance between the two selves doing the judging.

song.name: Song
song.definition: A sung passage standing outside the dialogue, free to say what the speaking characters cannot.

stage-property.name: Stage property
stage-property.definition: An object handled on stage that carries far more weight than its use in the scene explains.

symbolic-objects.name: Symbolic objects
symbolic-objects.definition: An object the narrative keeps returning to until it stands for the argument rather than illustrating it.

thresholds.name: Thresholds
thresholds.definition: Doors, windows, gates and stairs used to mark what may be crossed, by whom, and at what cost.
